interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the React Flight protocol and wire format?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: React Flight is the streaming wire format used to transmit React Server Components (RSC) to the client. It is a line-delimited stream where each line represents a chunk: 1) Model chunks (`M`): represent Client Component references (`{ id, chunks, name }`). 2) JSON chunks (`J`): represent element trees with props, children, and slots. 3) Promise chunks (`P`): represent suspended promises. The browser reconstructs the VDOM tree progressively without loading server-only JavaScript packages.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The cutting-edge Next.js App Router / RSC architecture question.

realWorldUseCases.description: Streaming server-rendered component trees over HTTP without sending server-side dependencies (like markdown parsers or database drivers) to the browser.

howToExplain.opening: The React Flight wire format is a line-delimited JSON stream that serializes Server Component trees, allowing clients to reconstruct UI progressively.
keyPoints: Zero bundle impact: server libraries are never sent to the browser.
Streams UI chunks as data resolves on the server.
Client component boundaries are serialized as module references ($).
Enables progressive streaming and concurrent hydration.
howToExplain.closingImpression: React Flight decouples backend computational complexity from client JavaScript bundle sizes.
analogies: Prefabricated housing: the factory builds and paints the walls on-site, shipping finished panels to the lot rather than shipping raw timber and sawmills.

commonMistakes.why: RSC returns the Flight stream (virtual DOM descriptions), NOT raw HTML. HTML is generated by SSR. Flight allows updating client state without losing client component state.
commonMistakes.correct: Clarify that RSC returns Flight JSON data, not HTML.

followUpDeepDive.question: Where in React source is the Flight Client implemented?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In `packages/react-client/src/ReactFlightClient.js` inside `parseModel()`, which converts wire strings into React elements.
